name: XTDB
tagline: Bitemporal SQL database on object storage that keeps every version of every row.
description: XTDB (originally Crux) is an immutable database from JUXT that records both system time and valid time for every row, so you can query what was true at any point and what the database believed at any point, including retroactive corrections. Version 2 is SQL-first: it speaks the PostgreSQL wire protocol and Arrow Flight SQL, stores columnar Apache Arrow data on object storage such as S3, and adds XTQL for Datalog-flavoured queries over semi-structured records. It fits audit-heavy domains such as finance, insurance and healthcare where reconstructing history is a requirement. Write throughput and ecosystem size are modest next to mainstream SQL engines.

pricing.notes: Open source; JUXT offers support and workshops.

scale.notes: Compute nodes scale out for reads on shared object storage; writes go through a single transaction log.

strengths: Native bitemporality: valid-time and system-time queries in standard SQL:2011 syntax
Immutable history makes audit and regulatory reconstruction straightforward
Columnar Arrow storage on S3-style object stores
Postgres wire compatibility for existing drivers and tools
weaknesses: Single transaction log limits write throughput
Smaller ecosystem and fewer managed options than Postgres
Bitemporal modelling has a learning curve
useCases: Financial and insurance systems needing as-of reporting
Event-sourced systems wanting SQL over history
notIdealFor: Simple CRUD where history is not needed
